correctness.rationale: For any selected powers, the AP step divides each difference; the exact gcd of base-power differences yields the sharp repunit index-span lower bound. Equality cases force consecutive exponents and maximal gcd step for at least three ones. Three or more ones also force exponent diameter at most twice the base logarithm of the index span; a sampled factor is determined by the positions of its first two ones and their exponent gap, giving the quadratic-logarithmic count. Composite bases and all endpoints are covered; the standard-library checker confirms 19,448 finite exponent cases and 2,898,000 sampled windows without substituting them for proof.

value.rationale: The arithmetic-factor language of the sparse power-indicator word is a canonical object in combinatorics on automatic words. Its exact maximal Hamming-weight profile and rigid shortest witnesses are fully settled at every base and length, and the polynomial O(n^2 log n) bound gives a quantitatively stronger structural conclusion than the general effective-alphabet exp(o(n)) upper behavior. This is more than a selected finite table or a normalization of an already counted factor invariant; it depends on an exponent-configuration counting argument.
